taxonomyNote: NatureServe (McDonough et al. 2022) splits the eastern spotted skunk into S. putorius (Alleghanian, east of the Mississippi) and S. interrupta (plains spotted skunk); the ADW page predates the split.
fieldMarks: Small, weasel-like skunk with a small white spot on the forehead and one in front of each ear
Six distinct white stripes on the front of the body; rear body has two interrupted white bands
White spot each side of the rump and two at the tail base
Front claws sharp, recurved and more than twice as long as hind claws
behavior: Mostly nocturnal; mostly inactive in winter
Opportunistic omnivore: small mammals, grubs and insects, corn, grapes, berries
Dens in abandoned burrows, brush piles, hollow logs or trees, rock crevices and under buildings
habitat: Prefers forested areas or habitats with significant cover; ADW also gives wooded areas, tall-grass prairie and rocky habitats.
range: NatureServe places S. putorius east of the Mississippi River, from the Florida peninsula north to at least Pennsylvania.

lookalikes.name: Western spotted skunk
lookalikes.howToTell: White areas more extensive on the western species.
